title: Little Office of S. John Nepomucene, Martyr, The Singular Patron of Penitents and Those in Danger of Reputation

introductoryNotes.text: From a book of the same name published in 1741.

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.
℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.
Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Sidus orbis, et decori Fax Joannes Aetheris; Qui Bohemis es favori, Et Patronus singulis!
blocks.english:
Star of the world, and torch
Of the beautiful heavens, John,
Who art a favour to the Bohemians
And patron of each!

blocks.source: Tua felix Nepomucium Vidit incunabula; Teque tota gens Amicum Credit ab que fabula.
blocks.english:
Happy Nepomuk beheld
Thy cradle,
And the whole people believes thee its friend,
[The printed “ab que fabula” is unresolved.]
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “ab que fabula”; this clause remains unresolved.

blocks.source: Magna Proles Zachariae Nascitur miraculo: Precibusque Tu Mariae Impetraris saeculo.
blocks.english:
The great offspring of Zachary
Is born by a miracle;
And thou, through Mary’s prayers,
Art obtained for the world.

blocks.source: Mox futuram claritatem Rutilantes flammulae; Atque vitae sanctitatem Praenotarunt stellulae.
blocks.english:
Little shining flames
Soon foretold thy future brightness,
And little stars
The holiness of thy life.
Antiphon (Isaiae 49)

blocks.source: Dominus ab utero vocavit me: de ventre matris meae recordatus est nominis mei.
blocks.english: The Lord called me from the womb; from my mother’s womb He remembered my name.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.english: ℣. Unto Thee have I lifted up my soul.

blocks.source: ℟. Deus meus in Te confido, non erubescam.
blocks.english: ℟. My God, in Thee I trust; let me not be ashamed.
℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad Te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Ominpotens sempiterne Deus, cui soli omnis honor et gloria debetur; per gloriosa Sancti Tui Martyris Joannis Nepomuceni merita, Te supplices exoramus, ut omnem a nobis publicam infamiam et ignominiam clementer avertas, concedasque, ut cum honore sic transeamus per bona temporalia, ut non amittamus aeterna. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui Tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Almighty everlasting God, to whom alone all honour and glory are due, through the glorious merits of Thy holy Martyr John Nepomucene we humbly beseech Thee mercifully to turn away from us all public disgrace and dishonour, and grant that we may so pass with honour through temporal goods as not to lose the eternal. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who with Thee liveth and reigneth in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Ominpotens” is retained in Latin; Almighty is its provisional reading.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Tua primum cum juventa Consecratur literis, Docta stillant mox fluenta Suada prodit fertilis.
blocks.english:
When thy youth is first
Consecrated to learning,
Learned streams soon flow;
Fruitful eloquence comes forth.

blocks.source: In Palaestris praedicari Jus bibisse Canonum; Doctor ergo nominaris, Nova lux fidelium.
blocks.english:
In the schools, [the printed “praedicari” is uncertain],
Thou hast drunk the law of the canons;
Therefore thou art named Doctor,
A new light of the faithful.
blocks.editorialNote: “In Palaestris praedicari Jus bibisse Canonum” is compressed; the position of “praedicari” is uncertain.

blocks.source: Presbyter post haec es unctus, Praeco sacris pulpitis: Hoc honore rite functus, Sacra promis dogmata.
blocks.english:
After this thou art anointed priest,
A herald in sacred pulpits;
Rightly exercising this honour,
Thou dost declare holy doctrines.

blocks.source: Factus Aulae castigatur, Luxus et licentia, Stolidique reprobatur, Saeculi dementia.
blocks.english:
[The printed “Factus Aulae castigatur” is grammatically defective.]
Luxury and licence are chastised,
And the madness
Of the foolish world is reproved.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Factus Aulae castigatur” has defective syntax; no missing title or subject is invented.

blocks.english: Antiphon (Jerem. 1)
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo, et universa, quaecunque mandavero tibi, loqueris.
blocks.english: Behold, I have put My words in thy mouth, and thou shalt speak all that I shall command thee.
℣. O God, depart not far from me.

blocks.source: ℟. Deus meus in auxilium meum respice.
blocks.english: ℟. My God, look unto my help.

blocks.source: Oremus, Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, ut supra.
blocks.english: Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, as above.

Hymn

blocks.source: Imperator ipse morum Iractus innocentia, Minor hostis tunc proborum, Tibi spondet ardua.
blocks.english:
The emperor himself, angered
By the innocence of thy conduct,
[The printed “Minor hostis tunc proborum” is unresolved],
Promises thee high things.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Iractus” and “Minor hostis tunc proborum”; the first is provisional and the latter clause unresolved.

blocks.source: Sed ad alta cur vocatus Promoveri respuis? Insulae cur deputatus Viliora respicis?
blocks.english:
But why, called to high things,
Dost thou reject advancement?
Why, appointed to an island,
Dost thou regard lesser things?
blocks.editorialNote: The source visibly prints “Insulae.” Island is retained literally rather than silently substituting a mitre or bishopric.

blocks.source: Nempe totus ad superna Spiritus cum vertitur: Terra mundus ut caverna Merito contemnitur:
blocks.english:
Surely, when the spirit turns
Wholly toward things above,
The earth, the world, as a cavern
Is rightly despised;

blocks.source: Hinc in Aula dividebas Pauperum stipendia, Et egenis conferrebas Deputata munera.
blocks.english:
Hence in the court thou didst distribute
The sustenance of the poor,
And bestow upon the needy
The appointed gifts.
Antiphon (Galat. 6)

blocks.source: Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi: per quem mihi mundus crucifixus est, et ego mundo.
blocks.english: But far be it from me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world is crucified to me and I to the world.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: ℣. Suscipe me Domine secundum eloquium tuum et vivam.
blocks.english: ℣. Uphold me, O Lord, according to Thy word, and I shall live.

blocks.source: ℟. Et non confundas me ab expectatione mea.
blocks.english: ℟. And confound me not in my expectation.
Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, etc.

blocks.source: Interim flagitiorum Pestis Aulam polluit: Quando Wenceslaus, horum Fautor, ipsis adstruit.
blocks.english:
Meanwhile the plague of crimes
Pollutes the court,
When Wenceslaus, their patron,
Adds to them.

blocks.source: Imperatrix ast Mariti Intuens licentiam: Vana spernens, corde miti Servat innocentiam.
blocks.english:
But the empress, beholding
Her husband’s licence,
Despising vanities, with a meek heart
Keeps her innocence.

blocks.source: Cui jactae tot procellis Montis adstas Arbiter; Animique moesta pellis Ceu coruscus Lucifer.
blocks.english:
For her, tossed by so many storms,
Thou dost stand as arbiter of the mountain,
And dispel the sadness of her soul
Like a shining morning star.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Montis adstas Arbiter.” The literal mountain/arbiter wording is retained provisionally rather than replacing it with an external account of his confessional ministry.

blocks.source: Sed Tribunal cum verendum Pia saepe visiteret: Crescit ardor ad ascendium, Toties quid proderet?
blocks.english:
But when she piously visited
The reverend tribunal often,
[The printed “Crescit ardor ad ascendium” is uncertain.]
What would it yield so often?
blocks.editorialNote: “ad ascendium” and the final question are defective or ambiguous; the English remains provisional.

blocks.english: Antiphon (Act. 20)

blocks.source: Non facio animam meam pretiosiorem quam me, dummodo consummem cursum meum.
blocks.english: I do not make my soul more precious than myself, so long as I may finish my course.
℣. Help me, O Lord my God.

blocks.source: ℟. Salvum me fac secundum misericordiam tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. Save me according to Thy mercy.
Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, etc.

blocks.source: Ampla spes est dignitatum, Munerandus diceris, Caesari si vis reatum Aperire Conjugis.
blocks.english:
Great is the hope of dignities;
Thou art told thou shalt be rewarded
If thou wilt reveal to Caesar
The guilt of his wife.

blocks.source: Sed nefanda postulantis Cum favorem despicis: Aestuantis et minantis Tonat ira Caesaris.
blocks.english:
But when thou dost despise the favour
Of him who demands wicked things,
The wrath of Caesar thunders,
Seething and threatening.

blocks.source: Facibus perusta squallent In Catasta viscera: At secari tota mallent, Quam fateri credita.
blocks.english:
Scorched by torches, the body
Lies foul upon the rack;
Yet it would rather be wholly cut apart
Than confess what was entrusted.

blocks.source: Inde liber et solutus Rursus adstas publico: Mira post haec elocutus Spiritu prophetico.
blocks.english:
Then free and released,
Thou dost stand again before the public,
Afterwards speaking wondrous things
With a prophetic spirit.
Antiphon (Rom. 8 [the printed parenthesis is unclosed])

blocks.source: Non sunt condignae passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quae revelabitur in nobis.
blocks.english: The sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory which shall be revealed in us.

blocks.source: ℣. Intende anima mea, et libera eam.
blocks.english: ℣. Attend to my soul, and deliver it.
℟. Rescue me because of my enemies.
Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, etc.

blocks.source: Trux Tyrannus rursus ira Furis, instat, aestuat; Comminatus quaeque dira, Nisi jussis annuat.
blocks.english:
The fierce tyrant again rages in anger,
Presses on, and seethes,
Threatening every dreadful thing
Unless he yield to his commands.

blocks.source: Solito stat firma mentis More virtus jugiter: Ergo vinctus clam fluentis Mergitur crudeliter.
blocks.english:
The strength of his mind stands firm
Continually in its accustomed way;
Therefore, bound, he is secretly
And cruelly drowned in the waters.

blocks.source: Nocte Caesar cogitabat Facinus latescere; Sed serena lux natabat Martyris cum corpore.
blocks.english:
By night Caesar thought
His crime would lie hidden;
But a clear light floated
With the Martyr’s body.

blocks.source: Unde tota, copioso Praga viso lumine, Concitatur, et vadoso Corpus effert flumine.
blocks.english:
Hence all Prague, seeing
The abundant light,
Is stirred, and brings forth the body
From the shallow river.
Antiphon (Rom. 8)

blocks.source: Certus sum, quia neque mors, neque vita, neque Angeli, neque Principatus, neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a charitate Dei, quae est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro.
blocks.english: I am certain that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor any other creature shall be able to separate us from the charity of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
℣. In Thee, O Lord, have I hoped.
℟. Let me not be confounded for ever.
Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, etc.

blocks.source: Cathedrali collocatus Aede, Martyr plurimis Undequeque visitatus Rutilat miraculis.
blocks.english:
Placed in the cathedral church,
The Martyr, visited by very many
From every side,
Shines with miracles.

blocks.source: Hocce rarum praedicabit Posteris Religio: Mansit expers lingua tabis, Maximo prodigio.
blocks.english:
Religion shall proclaim
This rare thing to posterity:
His tongue remained free from decay,
A very great marvel.

blocks.source: Nempe viva quae tacendo Delictere voluit: Mira Caeli nunc loquendo Emitere meruit.
blocks.english:
For, while living, by keeping silence
It chose [the printed “Delictere” is unresolved];
Now by speaking the wonders of heaven
It merited [the printed “Emitere” is uncertain].
blocks.editorialNote: “Delictere” is unresolved, and “Emitere” uncertain; the source’s contrast between silence and speaking is retained.

blocks.source: Qui reatus crubescunt Consistendo prodere: Qui per acta pertimescunt Gravem famam perdere:
blocks.english:
Those who are ashamed
To disclose their guilt [the printed “Consistendo” is uncertain],
Those who through their deeds fear
To lose their weighty reputation,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “crubescunt” and “Consistendo” are defective. The shame reading is provisional and the latter word remains uncertain.

blocks.source: Huc recurrunt; ac honoris Constat his integritas: Anxiique mox pudoris Desinit perplexitas.
blocks.english:
Have recourse here; and the integrity
Of their honour stands firm,
And soon the perplexity
Of anxious shame ceases.

blocks.source: Laus perennis, et sonora Triadi sit gloria: Martyri per quam decora Obtigit victoria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise and resounding glory
Be to the Trinity,
Through whom an honourable victory
Fell to the Martyr.
Antiphon (Ps. 20)

blocks.source: Gloriam et magnum decorum imposuisti super eum, posuisti in capite ejus coronam de lapide pretioso.
blocks.english: Thou hast laid glory and great beauty upon him; Thou hast set upon his head a crown of precious stone.
℣. Give praise to the Lord, for He is good.
℟. For His mercy endures for ever.
Let us pray. Almighty everlasting God, etc.

blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Acliente” and “Praesto prone”; the client and readiness readings are provisional.

blocks.source: Pelle moestum cordis aestum, Aufer ignominiam: Perque fata duc beata Ad aeternam patriam. Amen.
blocks.english:
Drive away the sorrowful heat of my heart,
Remove dishonour,
And through a blessed end lead me
To my eternal homeland. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. The seven printed hours and commendation remain; no Lauds is introduced. Six collect incipits expand the full Matins collect within this office, without duplicating the printed concluding versicles. The story of the martyr’s tongue and other historical claims remain statements of the source.
